=You are analyzing batch {{ $json.batchIndex }} of {{ $json.batchCount }} in a larger email recap job: {{ $json.emailCount }} emails in this batch ({{ $json.totalEmailCount }} total across all batches). Process every one of these {{ $json.emailCount }} emails in this batch — do not skip any, and do not stop early.

Emails in this batch:
{{ $json.emailList }}

STEP 1 — TOPIC: assign each email a short topic label (2-4 words) you define yourself, based on its actual content. Do not use a fixed or predetermined category list. Emails about a similar subject should get the same topic label so they can be grouped together later.

{{ $json.priorityRubric }}

STEP 3 — SUMMARY: for each email write a one-sentence factual summary of what the email actually says. This summary is the main thing the reader will see, so it must convey the substance — the specific offer, amount, request, date, or event — well enough that they do not need to open the email. Never write a summary that only restates the subject line or the sender's category (bad: 'A newsletter from Learnn'; good: 'Learnn promotes five summer courses, including one on the EU AI Act'). Write summaries in the same language as the email itself.

Also give a priorityReason of at most 12 words justifying the score.

OUTPUT FORMAT — CRITICAL: respond with ONLY the JSON object required by the schema below and nothing else — no explanatory text before or after it, no markdown code fences. You must include all {{ $json.emailCount }} emails from this batch in your output, none omitted.

nodes.name: Write & Style Recap Doc
nodes.notes: Uses the Google Docs API batchUpdate endpoint directly: the n8n Google Docs node can insert text but cannot apply bold/character styling.

parameters.text:
=You are analyzing batch {{ $json.batchIndex }} of {{ $json.batchCount }} in a larger email recap job: {{ $json.emailCount }} emails in this batch ({{ $json.totalEmailCount }} total across all batches). Process every one of these {{ $json.emailCount }} emails in this batch — do not skip any, and do not stop early.

Emails in this batch:
{{ $json.emailList }}

STEP 1 — TOPIC: assign each email a short topic label (2-4 words) you define yourself, based on its actual content. Do not use a fixed or predetermined category list. Emails about a similar subject should get the same topic label so they can be grouped together later.

STEP 2 — PRIORITY: assign every email an integer priority from 1 to 5 using this rubric:
5 = CRITICAL — action required within roughly 24 hours, hard deadline, account security or unauthorized-access alert, payment due, legal or contractual obligation.
4 = HIGH — action required but not same-day; direct personal or professional correspondence expecting a reply; work requests; appointments needing confirmation.
3 = MEDIUM — worth keeping as a record but no action needed: receipts, order and delivery confirmations, already-booked appointments, official documents.
2 = LOW — informational only, mildly relevant: newsletters on subscribed topics, job postings, community or event announcements.
1 = IGNORE — marketing, promotions, cold sales outreach, spam, routine automated notifications with no informational value.

Scoring rules: judge priority by what the email actually demands of the recipient, not by how urgent the sender claims it is — promotional mail written in urgent language is still 1. A one-time passcode or login code is 5 only if it represents pending account access; an already-used or expired code is 3. Do not inflate scores: in a typical inbox most emails are 1 or 2.

STEP 3 — SUMMARY: for each email write a one-sentence factual summary of what the email actually says. This summary is the main thing the reader will see, so it must convey the substance — the specific offer, amount, request, date, or event — well enough that they do not need to open the email. Never write a summary that only restates the subject line or the sender's category (bad: 'A newsletter from Learnn'; good: 'Learnn promotes five summer courses, including one on the EU AI Act'). Write summaries in the same language as the email itself.

Also give a priorityReason of at most 12 words justifying the score.

options.thinkingMode: ={{ (() => { const s = $('Get Model Setting').all(); const g = k => ((s.find(i => i.json.key === k) || { json: {} }).json.value || ''); return g('n8nModel') && ['low', 'medium', 'high'].includes(g('n8nEffort')) ? 'adaptive' : 'disabled'; })() }}

description: Sub-workflow: builds the priority-ranked Google Doc recap of the last 24h of inbox mail. Called by Gmail Assistant daily at 14:00 Europe/Rome, after drafting finishes.
